drhp.one_liner: Grovy India Limited is a BSE-listed, Delhi-based real estate developer established in 1985 that specialises in premium residential redevelopment — boutique builder floors and low-rise luxury residences — in South Delhi and Lutyens' Delhi, with 150+ projects delivered.

Commercial: Select Boutique Commercial Developments (strategic commercial spaces complementing residential projects, mixed-use community value in established South Delhi neighbourhoods)
Construction / Residential: Premium Builder Floors (flagship offering — independently designed floors with structured development amenities)
Low-Rise Luxury Residences (boutique developments targeting HNIs and NRIs)

risks.note: Every disclosed project — completed, on-going and pipeline — sits in a handful of South Delhi colonies (East of Kailash, Greater Kailash 1 and 2, Hauz Khas, Anand Niketan, Neeti Bagh, Defence Colony, Gulmohar Park, Safdarjung Enclave), and management explicitly states the addressable market is large enough to grow 'without geographic diversification'. The same supply constraint the Company treats as its moat also means there is no second market to fall back on if South Delhi pricing, redevelopment economics or FAR/building norms turn adverse.
risks.risk: Extreme geographic and product concentration in South Delhi / Lutyens' Delhi residential redevelopment

risks.note: Management lists 'economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures and adverse macroeconomic developments affecting consumer sentiment and investment activity' among key risks. Ultra-luxury housing is a discretionary, sentiment-driven purchase, so an HNI/NRI confidence shock hits sales velocity and realisations directly.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic slowdown and inflation depressing luxury housing demand

risks.note: Listed as a key risk: 'changes in government policies, taxation laws, regulatory frameworks and real estate-related compliance requirements'. The Company's own economics depend on a favourable regime — enhanced FAR norms, elevator and stilt-parking provisions and improved building specifications are cited as what made redevelopment viable, so a reversal would compress the business model at its source.
risks.risk: Regulatory, policy and taxation change in real estate

risks.note: Explicitly flagged by management as a key risk for project execution. With eight on-going projects carrying dated deliveries between Q3 FY 2026-27 and Q4 FY 2027-28 and a stated ambition to run 20-25 projects a year, approval slippage directly threatens the delivery timetable and the on-time-handover reputation the Company names as its key differentiator.
risks.risk: Delays in statutory approvals, permissions and regulatory clearances

risks.note: Management flags 'fluctuations in the prices and availability of construction materials, labour and other critical resources'. Projects are executed against a pre-approved budget and construction plan, so input inflation between budgeting and completion is absorbed by the developer and erodes project margin.
risks.risk: Construction input cost and labour availability volatility

risks.note: Listed as a key risk: 'changes in interest rates and liquidity conditions impacting borrowing costs and housing demand'. It bites at both ends — the Company reports a leveraged capital structure (debt-equity of 1.08 in FY26 versus 1.21 in FY25) alongside a stated intent to raise up to Rs 40 Crore, while buyer mortgage affordability moves the same way.
risks.risk: Interest-rate and liquidity risk on both borrowing cost and housing demand

risks.note: The business model rests on collaborating with individual landowners and families under redevelopment agreements and on deploying own capital alongside financial partners in a co-investment model, with on-going projects described as 'leveraging co-invested capital'. Execution and returns therefore depend on counterparties the Company does not control — landowner consent and partner funding availability — and the stated growth plan leans heavily on a single named capital relationship, Golden Growth Fund.
risks.risk: Dependence on partner capital and on structured redevelopment agreements with individual landowners

risks.note: Management flags 'increased competition within the real estate sector and changing customer preferences'. Redevelopment opportunities in South Delhi are open to any developer able to strike a landowner agreement, so competitive intensity can bid up acquisition terms even as buyer taste for design, sustainability and smart-home features keeps moving.
risks.risk: Competition and shifting customer preferences in a market with no supply moat on the demand side

currentContext.expansion: Grovy is a relatively asset-light real-estate developer, so its 'expansion' is a project pipeline rather than plant capex. The FY26 annual report describes the Company as entering a new phase of expansion driven by redevelopment opportunities, strategic capital partnerships and premium-housing demand in South Delhi, and sets out growth pillars: expanding the redevelopment footprint across South Delhi and Lutyens' Delhi, scaling execution to a target of 20-25 projects annually over the next three years supported by stronger project-management systems, vendor relationships and technology-driven monitoring, and leveraging the strategic partnership with Golden Growth Fund (a Category-II AIF) to accelerate project acquisitions. The Company states it is evaluating fund-raising of up to Rs 40 Crore, subject to necessary approvals, to strengthen the balance sheet and participate in a larger number of redevelopment opportunities, and separately intends to pursue a listing of its equity shares on the NSE, subject to regulatory approvals and eligibility. On the ground, the disclosed portfolio comprises five residential projects shown as Completed (East of Kailash 10,000 sq. ft and four at Greater Kailash 1 of 20,000 / 10,000 / 22,000 / 15,000 sq. ft, the last carrying a Q4 FY 2025-26 delivery marker); eight on-going developments with dated deliveries — Greater Kailash 2 (15,000 sq. ft, Q3 FY 2026-27), Anand Niketan (17,000 sq. ft, Q3 FY 2026-27), Greater Kailash 1 (20,000 sq. ft, Q4 FY 2026-27), Hauz Khas (15,000 sq. ft, Q1 FY 2027-28), Hauz Khas (15,000 sq. ft, Q3 FY 2027-28), Greater Kailash 1 (20,000 sq. ft, Q3 FY 2027-28), Neeti Bagh (36,000 sq. ft, Q3 FY 2027-28) and Greater Kailash 1 (15,000 sq. ft, Q4 FY 2027-28); and an upcoming pipeline of four undated (TBD) redevelopment projects — two at Defence Colony (15,000 sq. ft each), Gulmohar Park (20,000 sq. ft) and Safdarjung Enclave (20,000 sq. ft) — described as being finalised for launch, with the broader pipeline earmarked for launch in FY 2026-27. Ongoing projects are described as leveraging co-invested capital, consistent with the Company's stated model of deploying its own capital alongside financial partners across land acquisition, construction and completion, with controlled project sizes and phased development to reduce financial risk. The report discloses no rupee capital-expenditure quantum and no manufacturing capacity.
